title: check-doc-links
responsibility: Owns the check-doc-links build or maintenance script.

inputs.name: markdownLinks.source
inputs.description: The full text of one Markdown document, split on newlines and scanned for inline `[text](target)` links outside fenced code blocks and inline code spans. Reference-style links are not recognized, while an image such as `![alt](src)` is matched like any other link.
examples:
# Setup

Read [the boundaries](ARCHITECTURE-BOUNDARIES.md#layers) first.

[Upstream](https://example.com/docs)
See [the README](README.md) and `[not a link](README.md)` for details.

inputs.name: codePaths.source
inputs.description: The full text of one Markdown document, scanned line by line for backticked repository paths outside fenced code blocks. A match needs a `src/`, `test/`, `scripts/`, `packages/` or `crates/` prefix and a file extension, so a bare name such as `README.md` is never listed.
examples:
# Owners

| Owner | File |
| --- | --- |
| Core | `src/core/files.ts` |
| Scripts | `scripts/check-doc-links.ts` |
Keep `README.md` short and link to `scripts/check-doc-links.ts`.

inputs.name: headingAnchors.source
inputs.description: The full text of one Markdown document; only its ATX headings, meaning lines that start with one to six `#` characters followed by whitespace, produce anchors, and headings inside fenced code blocks are ignored. Setext (underlined) headings are not recognized.

inputs.name: brokenDocLinks.documents
inputs.description: The repository-relative paths where the run starts, each checked once in list order, and a listed path that does not exist is reported as a problem. Each link target that exists, ends in `.md` and is not the linking document itself is queued and checked the same way, so linked Markdown files are followed through their own links too.

inputs.name: brokenDocLinks.files
inputs.description: The adapter for every lookup: `exists(path)` reports whether a repository-relative path exists and `read(path)` returns its text, and `read` is only called for a path that `exists` has already confirmed. `main` passes Node's `existsSync` and a `readFileSync` wrapper that decodes UTF-8.

inputs.name: brokenDocLinks.pathChecked
inputs.description: The documents whose backticked repository paths must also exist; for each listed document that is checked, every `codePaths` target is tested with `exists` and a missing one is reported. It defaults to `[]`, which checks no code paths, and `main` passes `pathCheckedDocuments`.

outputs.name: checkedDocuments
outputs.description: The documents every run checks first, in this order: `ARCHITECTURE-BOUNDARIES.md`, then `README.md`. Markdown files that they link to are checked after them, so this list is only the starting set and not every file the run checks.

outputs.name: pathCheckedDocuments
outputs.description: The documents whose backticked repository paths must also exist, because they map owners to files; `main` passes this list as the `pathChecked` argument of `brokenDocLinks`. In this module it holds only `ARCHITECTURE-BOUNDARIES.md`.

outputs.name: markdownLinks
outputs.description: The inline links found in one document, in document order, each with its 1-based line number and its target (the text up to the first whitespace, `>` or closing parenthesis), such as `README.md` or `#layers`. External URLs are included, and `brokenDocLinks` skips them without fetching anything.

outputs.name: codePaths
outputs.description: The backticked repository paths in one document outside fenced code blocks, in document order, each with its 1-based line number and its path without the backticks. Only paths that begin with `src/`, `test/`, `scripts/`, `packages/` or `crates/` and end in a file extension are included.

outputs.name: headingAnchors
outputs.description: The GitHub-style anchor slugs for the ATX headings of one document: the text is lowercased, characters other than letters, digits, whitespace, `_` and `-` are dropped, each whitespace character becomes a hyphen, and a repeated slug gets a `-1`, `-2` suffix. `brokenDocLinks` checks each decoded, lowercased `#fragment` of a link to a `.md` file against the set computed for that file.

outputs.name: brokenDocLinks
outputs.description: One line per problem, starting with the document and, except for a missing checked document, its line number; the problems are a missing checked document, a missing backticked path, a link that leaves the repository, a missing link target and a missing heading. The list is sorted with JavaScript's default string sort, and an empty array means that every checked link and checked backticked path resolves.
examples: README.md:7: ARCHITECTURE-BOUNDARIES.md#layers has no such heading
